lines.text: I wrote it. Twice. I knew exactly how to ask for what I wanted, and exactly why somebody ought to refuse.

lines.text: The first time, I heard her call and answered. A student heard me from the stair. Another heard me inside a locked practice room. I was here, on this glass.

I do not know what would have followed my answer into those rooms. I want the tape anyway. Both facts belong to me.
I can care about you and still need the whole cost before any other request.

lines.text: I do not know what happens to all of us. Anyone who tells you they know is selling something.

choices.text: Tell me what to do and I will fix it.

lines.text: Please do not make yourself into the person who can fix everybody. This place loves that person.

lines.text: The person in the cleared room would risk leaving, even if they might end. You kept saying they would lose their home.

choices.text: Tell me what you stand to keep.

lines.text: Before you ask: yes, I want to keep my home. I want the stairs where I knew who was coming by the way they took them. I want that stupid draught under the practice-room door.
I am not outside this. I do not get to sound noble about it.

choices.text: Why can you not save it yourself?
Is that why you wanted the cassette back? To make me care?

lines.text: Because a dead person cannot promise a living future. This is all the future I have.
Ren lifts their intact hand. The other side follows a moment late and folds back into the body.

choices.text: And the cassette? Why ask me for that before this?

lines.text: I wanted the cassette. That part is true. I also knew that if you saw me wanting something small, you might stay for the large thing.
I am sorry. I can be lonely and calculating at the same time. You should know both before you answer.
I can care about you and still ask who has paid for this before.

choices.text: You were lonely. I would rather not hear what else you used me for.

lines.text: In the chamber room, there is a dated slip under the piano bench. The last guarantor wrote it herself. I kept it because she asked me to.
Read what she agreed to. Read what it cost her after she had already said yes. Do not take my summary.

lines.text: How else do you think music schools stay alive? It is not the money. There is none.

You read her slip. She knew the gate would not open. She did not know how long an ordinary missed day could stay with her. I was there when the photograph arrived.
One century is ending. I can make the next seal. I cannot be the person inside it.

choices.text: Those people deserve to be remembered. What did they know when they agreed?

choices.text: Then start again. Ask me plainly, and tell me the whole cost.

lines.text: Please help me keep this place standing.

choices.text: Explain the seal. Every part, before I answer.

lines.text: I will not. The roof is here. I am here. You can still leave.
I put my hand against your sternum. The missing part of me passes through you and closes round the school.
Your living name becomes its guarantor. For a hundred years this place cannot be demolished, sold out from under itself, or made empty by force.
The ordinary world will find ordinary reasons. A title that cannot be cleared. A foundation the survey missed. Someone refusing a signature. The protection is real. The reasons will be real too.
It does not repair the school. It does not feed anybody. People will still have to keep it alive. It only refuses the final destruction.

choices.text: What happens to me?

lines.text: You stay. In this building. In these grounds. The seal keeps your body alive, and the years outside keep going.
You can walk, eat, sleep, teach if anyone will listen. You can sit on this glass and watch the city. You cannot go home. Not for a visit. Not for a funeral.
The people you know will get older. The seal will not let you follow them out. At the end of the century it releases you. I do not know what the years it held back will do then.
I cannot reverse it once it closes. I cannot make that smaller by calling it a gift.

choices.text: If I say no, what happens right now?

lines.text: Yes. That is what I am asking. There is no kinder version hidden in the wording.

choices.text: Then tell me I can refuse.

lines.text: If you say no, I take my hand away. You keep the service key. You keep the choice to leave the roof and this building.

choices.text: I understand. Let me choose.

lines.text: SEAL, YEAR 0. M. VALE, CLEANER. I have been told that I will stay inside the grounds for one hundred years. I am signing while I can still walk away.

YEAR 61. The chamber roof leaked again. I changed the bucket before class. The seal kept the crews from taking the room. It never mended it for us.
